page: Microsoft Azure M16pds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The configuration features 16 dedicated vCPUs built on the 64-bit ARM64 processor architecture. Memory capacity is provisioned at 256 GB, resulting in an allocation ratio of 16 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance incorporates 945 GB of local NVMe SSD temporary storage and supports Azure Premium Storage. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are not included, and public IPv4 addresses are not bundled complimentary.

The M16pds_v4 pairs an ARM-based compute engine with substantial physical memory density. ARM64 architectures generally provide improved resource and power efficiency relative to traditional x86 server classes, lowering the cost profile per gigabyte of RAM for memory-constrained platforms. However, utilizing ARM hardware introduces platform compatibility requirements, necessitating binaries and dependencies compiled specifically for arm64 environments. Furthermore, the 945 GB local NVMe disk operates as scratch storage, meaning persistent data must rely on attached Premium Storage volumes.

Because of its 16:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and high-speed local NVMe scratch space, the M16pds_v4 is targeted at workloads that require large active data sets in memory rather than raw single-threaded compute strength. Typical deployment scenarios include in-memory databases such as Redis, relational database systems with expansive buffer pools, distributed caching nodes, memory-intensive data transformation jobs, and analytics workloads that leverage large in-memory tables.
description: Microsoft Azure M16pds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on a 64-bit ARM processor architecture running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs paired with 256 GB of system memory, yielding an extensive memory-to-core allocation of 16 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture consists of 945 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage alongside support for Azure Premium Storage, with no onboard GPU accelerators present. The use of ARM64 processors delivers high memory density with favorable compute resource efficiency, though workloads must be compiled for or natively support ARM instruction sets. Networking does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Given the high memory allocation, dedicated compute cores, and high-speed local NVMe disk, the M16pds_v4 is designed for memory-intensive workloads including in-memory databases, caching deployments, large operational databases, enterprise analytics, and data processing pipelines.
